title: Letter 9 — Attend to Yourself
attribution_note: Letter 9 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: What it means to attend to yourself

pairs.en: You ask me what it means: attend to yourself.
I answer.
You are called a Christian — but do you do the things that befit a Christian? Attend to yourself.
You confess God — but do you honour God with a good conscience? Attend to yourself.
In holy Baptism you renounced Satan and all his evil works — but have you not turned back after him, into an evil and corrupted life? Attend to yourself.
At your Baptism you promised to serve Christ, the Son of God, in faith and in righteousness — but do you remember your vows, and do you keep them? Attend to yourself.

sections.heading: Attend to the God who sees you, and who is silent no longer than He waits

pairs.en: You hear from the Word of God that God is in every place, and sees every deed, thought, undertaking and intention. Listen to what Holy Scripture says of this: *“Whither shall I go from Thy Spirit? or whither shall I flee from Thy presence?* *If I ascend up into heaven, Thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, Thou art there.* *If I ... dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea; even there shall Thy hand lead me, and Thy right hand shall hold me”* [Psalm 138:7, 10]. *“The eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.* *He knoweth all things ere ever they were created; so likewise after they were finished”* [Sirach 23:27–29]. Thine eyes, O Lord, *“are open upon all the ways of the sons of men: to give every one according to his ways”* [Jeremiah 32:19; Proverbs 15:3; Hebrews 4:13, and elsewhere]. Listen to what the wise Augustine says of this to God: “I confess, O Lord, that whatsoever I do, and whatever deed I do, I do it before Thee, and Thou seest all that I do far better than I myself, who do it. For whatsoever I do, Thou art equally always present, as the ever-watchful overseer of all my thoughts, intentions, delights and deeds.” And what Augustine confesses of himself, every man must likewise confess of himself. But do you, by your conduct, render Him honour in your deeds, your words, your undertakings and your intentions, as children render it to a father who is present, as servants to a master who is present, as subjects to a monarch who is present? Attend to yourself.

It is shameless, and an offence to a monarch, to misbehave before him. Every transgression, whether committed in deed, or word, or thought, is misconduct before God, and an offence to Him, and a harm to us. Attend to yourself.

Do you commit fornication in deed or in thought; do you steal and plunder; do you deceive, flatter, lie, speak evil, slander your neighbour, and commit other transgressions? — you misbehave before the eyes of God, and so act shamelessly before the majesty of God, and offend Him, and harm yourself. Consider this.
Do you lift up your heart to God in prayer? But do you not defile your heart with evil and unclean thoughts, and do you not harbour anger against your neighbour? Attend to yourself.
Do you lift up your hands to God? But do you not defile them with plunder, extortion and other unrighteousness? Attend to yourself.
Do you call upon the holy and dread name of God with your lips? But do you not stain them with foul speech, slander, condemnation, flattery, lying and other vices? Attend to yourself.

Do you stand before God in prayer with your body? But do you stand with your spirit? Do you bow before Him with your body? But do you bow with your spirit and your heart? Is it not one thing your tongue speaks in prayer, and another your mind is thinking? Attend to yourself.

sections.heading: Attend to the mercy you ask, and the mercy you give

pairs.en: Do you ask forgiveness of your sins from God? But do you yourself forgive your neighbour? Do you seek mercy from God? But do you yourself have mercy on your neighbour, a man like yourself? Do you say to God, “Hear me, O Lord!”? But do you yourself not stop your ears when your neighbour asks something of you? Attend to yourself. For such as we wish God to be toward us, such we ourselves must be toward our neighbours, and such as we are toward our neighbours, such will God be toward us. If we listen to our neighbours when they ask something of us, God listens to us. If we have mercy on the poor, our brethren, God has mercy on us, the poor. *“We forgive our debtors”* — God forgives us our debts. God attends to our mercy, and hears it, more than He hears the prayer we make with our lips, and He looks more upon a heart that is guileless, compassionate, merciful and generous, than upon the frequent repetition of “Lord, Lord.” For God is merciful and righteous: being merciful, He loves mercy, and has mercy on the one who shows mercy; and being righteous, He justly withholds His mercy from the one who himself will not show mercy. Read the parable of the debtor and his fellow-servant [Matthew 18:23–35], and you will see this truth.

sections.heading: Attend to the Benefactor by whom you live

pairs.en: You receive from God food, drink, clothing, a home and other good things — but do you remember the Benefactor, and do you thank Him from the heart? Attend to yourself. We are so poor and needy that we have nothing of our own, save our sins and our infirmities, and we receive so many benefits from our Creator that we cannot live even a single minute without Him. But when we sin, we thereby shamelessly offend this great Benefactor, and show ourselves ungrateful to Him. It is a heavy thing to offend a human benefactor; but how incomparably heavier to offend God, who is Himself all goodness and love, and who does not cease to do good even to those who do Him evil and offend Him! Attend to this.

Know for certain, friend, that it is better to die many times over than to offend God, the eternal Good, even in some small thing. Whoever sins against God, and so offends Him, does as one who receives every good thing from a human benefactor, but reviles him and dishonours him. Consider this, and attend to yourself.

sections.heading: Attend to Christ, who bought you with His own Blood

pairs.en: You know that Christ, the Son of God, redeemed you from the devil, from hell, and from eternal death, not with silver or gold, but with His own precious Blood — do you call to mind this great deed of His, past the mind's grasp? Do you remember it every day, and do you thank so great a Benefactor from a pure heart? Attend to yourself.
He did not spare His own Blood for your sake — do you not spare your money for the sake of His name?

He endured with all meekness reproach and slander for your sake — do you not take revenge for a reproachful and slanderous word against your neighbour, and do you endure it with meekness? Attend to yourself.
He suffered and died for your sake — do you show yourself ready for suffering and death for His sake? Attend to yourself.

He bore a most heavy cross, laden with your sins and the sins of the whole world — do you bear the cross that God has laid upon you, without murmuring and without indignation, but rather with thanksgiving, and do you follow Him? Attend to yourself.

*“Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example, that we should follow His steps.* *He did no sin, neither was guile found in His mouth: who, when He was reviled, reviled not again; when He suffered, He threatened not; but committed Himself to Him that judgeth righteously”* [1 Peter 2:21–23]. He drank the bitter cup for your sins, as the Gospel teaches — do you take pleasure in the sins for which Christ tasted such bitterness? Attend to yourself.
You call Him Lord. Truly He is Lord: *“The Lord is His name”* [Jeremiah 33:2]. But do you serve Him, as a servant serves his Lord? Attend to yourself.

He bought you to be His servant, not with silver or gold, but with His own Blood, as was said, and therefore you are “not your own,” but His purchased servant. Do you not live according to your own will, rather than His? Do you obey and do you please Him as your Lord, as the apostle says: *“Christ died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto Him which died for them, and rose again”* [2 Corinthians 5:15]? Attend to yourself.

He compels no one to please Him and to labour for Him, as the masters of this world do, but calls with love; and the love He has shown us, and the debt we owe Him as our Creator, our Lord and our Redeemer, and our highest Benefactor, persuade us of themselves. And that we please Him and labour for Him profits us, not Him. And if we do not do this, the harm is ours, not His. Attend to yourself.

He loved you, His enemy, so much that He did not refuse even to die for you — but do you love Him, who loves you, your Benefactor, so greatly? Attend to yourself. True love is known not by words, but by deeds; not by the frequent repetition of “Lord, Lord,” but by the doing of His will, according to His own word: *“He that hath My commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth Me”* [John 14:21].

sections.heading: Attend to your neighbour, who is set before you as your own self

pairs.en: Your neighbour is set before you as your own self, and you are commanded to love him as yourself. Do you love him? Do you not do to him what you would not wish done to yourself, and do you do to him what you would wish done to yourself? Do you rejoice with him when he rejoices, and grieve with him when he grieves? Do you suffer with him who suffers? Do you help him who is in distress? Do you strive to comfort him who is sorrowful? Do you wish to feed the hungry, to give drink to the thirsty, to clothe the naked, and to do the other works of mercy? And when you can, do you do them? And when you cannot, do you at least feel compassion for him in your heart? Attend to yourself.

We are all neighbours to one another: the rich to the poor, the healthy to the infirm, the wise to the unwise, the free to those shut up in prison, those in authority to those under them, and those under authority to those in authority, parents to their children and children to their parents, pastors to their people and people to their pastors, masters to their servants and servants to their masters, husbands to their wives and wives to their husbands, teachers to their pupils and pupils to their teachers, the old to the young and the young to the old. In a word, every man owes love to his neighbour, and all Christians are called *“by love to serve one another,”* in the apostle's word [Romans 13:8; Galatians 5:13].

sections.heading: Attend to your last hour, and to the Judgment

pairs.en: By the Word of God you have been called, and by the Blood of Christ redeemed, unto eternal life — do you take care for this? Do you seek it with all diligence? Are you not chasing after the vanity of this world? Does your heart not cling to this world? Do you remember that you are a stranger and a wayfarer in this world, as all godly people think of themselves? Attend to yourself.

You see that death seizes the young and the old, the prepared and the unprepared, in different ways — do you remember this hour, which all the saints remembered, and awaited with sighing, with tears and with repentance, and for which they so prepared themselves? Do you remember that hour, from which follows either to live for ever, or to die for ever; either to be in eternal blessedness, or in eternal torment; either to reign with Christ in heaven, or to be tormented with the devil and his angels in the fire of Gehenna — do you remember this dread hour? Attend to yourself.

You see that no one who dies takes anything with him from here, not riches, not honour, not glory, nor anything else, but leaves it all with the world. Do you remember that you too will leave everything, and that as you came naked into the world, so naked you shall go out from it? Attend to yourself.

That hour comes unlooked for, and sends the prepared and the unprepared alike into that age. Are you preparing for that hour, and are you striving now, in this present life, to be such as you would wish to be found in that hour? Do you wish to die a blessed death? Do you strive to live a godly life, to flee from every sin and to cling to every virtue, to call upon God with diligence and to please Him with faith and righteousness? Attend to yourself. For such as you shall be when you depart from this world, such shall you appear at the Judgment of Christ.

Christians draw near to the most holy Eucharist of the Body and Blood of Christ; this holy thing is given to the godly and to the holy, as the priest proclaims: “Holy Things for the holy.” How do you draw near to this great Mystery? With what faith and what conscience? Do you remember what the apostle wrote: *“let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup”* [1 Corinthians 11:28]? Attend to yourself. It is dreadful to approach unamended, and it is dreadful, too, to be cut off from it. Attend to this.

sections.heading: Attend to your calling and your place in life

pairs.en: Are you a ruler? How do you govern the people of God, your own brethren? Do you care for their common good? Do you root out injustice and plant righteousness? Do you restrain the self-will of the disorderly, and do you defend the innocent? Attend to yourself.
Are you under authority? Do you honour him who is set over you, and do you obey him for God's sake? Attend to yourself. *“For there is no power but of God”* [Romans 13:1].

Are you a judge? How do you judge men who are like yourself? Do you strive to search out the truth, and do you keep to what is right, as you promised before God? Do you not act against your conscience? Do you not justify the guilty, and condemn the innocent? Do you not show favour to persons in judgment? Do you not fear a man who is like yourself, though he be greater than you, more than you fear God? Do you remember that you too will stand before God's judgment? Attend to yourself.

If you are called to give witness in a court, how do you answer? Do you testify to men what your conscience testifies to you? Is it not one thing your conscience says, and another your tongue? Attend to yourself.

Are you a pastor? How do you shepherd the sheep of Christ, redeemed by His Blood? Do you feed them with the Word of God? Do you lead them by the example of a good life? Do you guard them from the spiritual beasts, the demons? Do you turn back those who have gone astray onto the way of truth, and so forth? Attend to yourself.

Are you among the flock? How do you conduct yourself toward your pastor? Do you honour him, do you love him, do you obey him? Do you show gratitude to him, who labours for you and seeks your salvation? Attend to yourself.

Are you a master? How do you deal with your servants and your peasants? Are they content with food and clothing? Do they have time to rest? Do you remember that as you wish to eat, drink, rest and be clothed, so do they too; that such flesh as you have, they have also; and that as your own suffering flesh feels pain, so does theirs? Do you remember this? Do you remember that you too have a Lord in the heavens, with whom there is no respect of persons, before whose judgment you will stand together with your servants and your peasants, and give account for how you dealt with them? Attend to yourself.
Are you a servant? How do you serve your master? Do you please him only when he is watching? Do you obey him, and do you carry out his commands with a good conscience? Attend to yourself.
Are you a father? How do you deal with your children? Do you teach them the fear of God? Do you raise them in the Christian calling? Do you show them an example of good deeds? Attend to yourself.
Are you a son or a daughter? Do you honour your father and your mother, as God commands? Attend to yourself.

Husband and wife! How do you deal with one another? Do you keep the fidelity of marriage faithfully? Do you love one another? Do you remember that you are *“one flesh”* [Ephesians 5:31; Genesis 2:24]? Attend to yourselves.

Are you rich? How, and on what, do you spend your riches? Do you remember that they are God's good gift, given you not for your own whims and luxury, but for your own need and your neighbour's? Do you remember that you are a *“steward”* and an administrator, and not the owner [Luke 16:1]? For all things are God's: *“The earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof”* [Psalm 23:3]. How do you spend God's good things? Do you provide for the poor and the needy, the people of God? Do you remember that you must give account of the riches given you? Do you remember that riches squandered on luxury and on whims perish, but riches given into the hands of the poor and the needy are preserved, and return to the giver with great increase in eternal life [Luke 14:13–14; Psalm 40:2–4; Mark 9:41]? Attend to yourself.

Are you poor, and do you receive alms? How, and on what, do you spend the alms given you for Christ's sake? On your need, or on luxury and whims? Do you not serve love of money and mammon under the appearance of poverty? Do you not gather riches from alms? Do you not rob the truly poor and needy of what is theirs? Do you not pretend to be poor, while having enough? Do you not pretend to be infirm, while being in health? Do you not live in idleness, and so have nothing to live on? Attend to yourself.

Are you a merchant? How do you buy and sell? Do you not sell poor goods as good, and cheap goods as dear? Do you not ask a higher price for your wares than they are worth? Do you not deceive your neighbour in selling, what you would not wish done to yourself? Do you not call upon the holy and dread name of God in a false oath, for the sake of some vile profit? Attend to yourself.

Are you learned, and do you have the gift of teaching? How, and to what end, do you use the talent given you by God? Do you seek from it the glory of God and the profit of your neighbour? Attend to yourself.

In a word — every Christian! How do you conduct yourself before God, who watches over all? How do you speak, act and think; with what heart do you deal with your neighbour? How, and on what, do you spend the time given you by God for repentance? Do you not waste it in idleness and empty amusements? Do you remember that time is precious, and that, like a word once spoken, once lost it does not return? Do you remember that the longer you live, the nearer you draw to death, to the Judgment of Christ, and to eternity, and that every man will most certainly go either into blessed or into tormented eternity? Attend to yourself!
Remember also this, O my soul: what you counsel your neighbour, do you yourself do it? Attend to yourself!
This, then, is what it means: attend to yourself. Remember this, consider it, and attend to yourself, that you may be saved.
Be saved in Christ.
